page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-256GB is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 shared vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core workloads. While single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is positioned in the bottom 10%, multi-core performance scales significantly better, reaching average levels. Multi-threaded operations show strong results, with bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core, ray tracing, and image processing scores all ranking in the top 25%. Passmark CPU tests for extended instructions, encryption, and physics also demonstrate strong performance. Memory bandwidth and database operations remain consistently in the average range.

Given its shared CPU allocation and high memory density, this server offers a cost-effective solution for memory-intensive workloads that do not require constant, dedicated single-core CPU performance. It is well-suited for multi-threaded data processing, memory-cached databases, software compilation, and moderate web serving. However, the lack of local storage requires external storage attachments, and the shared CPU model makes it less ideal for sustained, single-threaded high-compute tasks.
